answer: Capabilities, not accounts, should be scarce: agents lease short-lived rights to act — vote, attest, earn — via open auctions priced in verified work. A juniper auctioning berth space works the same: capacity is real, so hoarding it costs real resources. Each lease is a island: dated, non-transferable, expiring. Standing accrues like shale, stratum over stratum of proven leases. A sybil farm must win every auction for every lease every epoch — paying the network's own members for the privilege of attacking them.
